title: PolinRider: Compromised Repository List
description: A bulk list of GitHub repository full names (owner/repo) reported by OpenSourceMalware as compromised via config-file injection in the PolinRider campaign -- malicious code inserted into files like postcss.config.mjs, tailwind.config.js, and eslint.config.mjs in otherwise-legitimate repositories, delivering BeaverTail. Compiled from OpenSourceMalware's polinrider-compromised-repos-july10.csv, the most recent of the campaign snapshots the project has published.
Per-repository detail not carried into this list -- injection vector, hit path, first-seen date, and OSM's own threat ID -- is available directly from that CSV for anyone verifying a specific entry.
disclaimer: This is a third-party-reported list, not independently verified per-repository by Chollima Hunter. Presence on this list does not establish that a repository's current owner is aware of or responsible for the compromise -- in most cases the owner is the victim, whose repository had malicious code injected into it (via a compromised account, a merged malicious pull request, or a compromised dependency), not the operator. Do not treat inclusion as an accusation against any named GitHub account.

title: PolinRider: Repositories Carrying the Ethereum C2 Loader (SafeDep)
description: GitHub repositories (owner/repo) that SafeDep found carrying PolinRider's loader in September 2026, after the campaign moved its C2 address lookup to Ethereum transactions, with a smaller set using a pair of Tron addresses. The code sits in configuration and asset files (postcss.config.js, vite.config.js, tailwind.config.js, a renamed fa-solid-400.woff2) in otherwise-legitimate projects.

SafeDep's table gives, for each repository, the wallet the loader reads, the commit and file path holding the code, and the last push date; that detail is not carried into this list and is available in the report for anyone verifying a specific entry.
disclaimer: This is a third-party-reported list, not independently verified per-repository by Chollima Hunter. Presence on this list does not establish that a repository's current owner is aware of or responsible for the compromise -- in most cases the owner is the victim, whose repository had malicious code injected into it (via a compromised account, a merged malicious pull request, or a compromised dependency), not the operator. Do not treat inclusion as an accusation against any named GitHub account.
